Latin word

ē

ē, ex (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative; ex before vowels and often before consonants, ē only before consonants

from (out of); off (getting down from); out of, from

In this lexicon

  • from

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 35.3: venit ad nōs ex iīs quōs amāmus … gaudium

  • off

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 34: ex equō nōn dēscendere

  • out of

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās; Plin. NH 9.92: exīre ē marī in lacūs

  • ē cōnspectū abīre: disappear

    classical

  • ē lectulō extrahere: drag out of bed

    modern

  • ē trāmine dēscendere: get off

    our formation

  • ē birotā dēscendere: get off

    modern

  • aqua ē fistulā: tap water

    our formation

Examples

  • Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastigia.

    Come out of the kitchen, will you, you rascal.Plaut. Most. 1
